question: The tracked-vs-GSR positions differ by +2-3 m along pitch width in the far half (132831, 132877). Which side carries it?

step_1_pixel_space.test: GSR image foot points (u,v) of GSR frame 18930 (aligned -21) drawn on the 990753 panorama frame at match second 758
step_1_pixel_space.result: all 22 GSR points sit on the players' feet; the 65 official landmark pixels sit on the line intersections
step_1_pixel_space.conclusion: GSR pixel coordinates ARE in the panorama pixel space (the earlier 'not panorama pixels' note was wrong; the planar-homography failure below is because the stitched panorama is not planar)

step_2_gsr_mapping_vs_official_markings.method: smooth cubic polynomial image->pitch fitted on 30k GSR (u,v)->(x,y) pairs per match, evaluated at the 65 official landmark pixels against their official pitch coordinates

verdict: relative to the official painted markings, the GSR pitch coordinates are biased by several metres along pitch width (growing toward the far half); our landmark TPS honours the markings. The +2-3 m tracked-vs-GSR offset therefore sits mainly on the GSR side. Consequence for the scorecard: GSR-based 'matched players per frame' and 'defensive line error' UNDERSTATE our accuracy; team-colour and block-label agreement are affected little (bias is along width, block depth is along length).
caveats: the cubic map has 1-1.7 m self-residual and landmarks near the hull edge extrapolate; inside the hull the error is still 6-9 m, far above that
pixel-space identity verified visually on one frame (22 points) for 132831; 132877 inferred from identical image size (4096x1084) and the same offset signature
117092 (night) GSR images are 3840x1504 vs the 3840x1906 panorama, a different crop; its position-based figures were measured earlier and are not re-interpreted here
supersedes: the 'retraction' entry in venue-132831-detector-and-geometry.json (GSR pixels not panorama pixels) — that was wrong
